![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039710/assets/2abec0420bf322120bb37135af682a7bc04c97c86d7bf1bdfd04012a8355883c.png)

Consider the segment $\overline{PQ}$ above, and the transformation $\mathbf T$ defined as

$$
x = u - v + 7, \qquad y = u + v +1.
$$

The image of $\overline{PQ}$ under the action of $\mathbf T$ is the segment $\overline{P'Q'}$ in the $xy$-plane. Find $\overline{P'Q'}.$
e-12425.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $\mathbf T:\mathbb R^2\rightarrow\mathbb R^2$ is a function of the form

$$
\mathbf x = A \mathbf u + \mathbf b,
$$

where $\mathbf x, \mathbf u,$ and $\mathbf b$ are column vectors in $\mathbb R^2,$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that we can express the given transformation as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}u-v+7 \\ u+v+1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u-v \\ u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

The transformation $\mathbf T$ maps the endpoints of $\overline{PQ}$ to the endpoints of $\overline{P'Q'}.$ So, to find the image of $\overline{PQ},$ we find the images of each endpoint.

To quickly carry out this calculation, we set up the following matrices:

- The matrix $U$ containing the endpoints of our segment:

$$
[\begin{aligned}-5 & -5 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ that has the same shape as $U$ and with the vector $\mathbf b$ in each column:

$$
[\begin{aligned}7 & 7 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

The image of $\mathbf u$ under $\mathbf T$ is given by $A\mathbf u + \mathbf b.$ So, by applying $\mathbf T$ to $U,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AU+B & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-5 & -5 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}7 & 7 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-7 & -10 \\ -3 & 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}7 & 7 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the endpoints of the image in the $xy$-plane are $(0,-2)$ and $(-3,1).$

e-12426.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Polygon Under an Affine Transformation
e-12426.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039710/assets/dd8b1407add93e72afccf2138cc818df63d47fdaa6ccc23e843a5602d8c1dbd8.png)

          

Consider the rectangle $\Delta$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
\Delta  = \big\{ (u,v) \: : \: -1 \leq u \leq 1, \: -1\leq v \leq 1 \big\}.
$$

The transformation $\mathbf T$ is defined as

$$
x = u - v + 1, \qquad y = u+v
$$

Find the image of $\Delta$ in the $xy$-plane under the action of $\mathbf T.$
e-12426.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $\mathbf T:\mathbb R^2\rightarrow\mathbb R^2$ is a function of the form

$$
\mathbf x = A \mathbf u + \mathbf b,
$$

where $\mathbf x, \mathbf u,$ and $\mathbf b$ are column vectors in $\mathbb R^2,$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that we can express the given transformation as 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}u-v+1 \\ u+v\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u-v \\ u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

The transformation $\mathbf T$ maps the boundary of $\Delta$ to the boundary of the image. So, to find the image of $\Delta,$ we find the images of each side.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039710/assets/69d92e24d5b0c81e54d3878793efe7c07d16fc963222997fe4fec4ffb3f93bd5.png)

          

To quickly carry out this calculation, we set up the following matrices:

- The matrix $U$ containing all vertices of our square:

$$
[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ -1 & -1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ that has the same shape as $U$ and with the vector $\mathbf b$ in each column:

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

The image of $\mathbf u$ under $T$ is given by $A\mathbf u + \mathbf b.$ So, by applying $\mathbf T$ to $U,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AU+B & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ -1 & -1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 0 & -2 \\ -2 & 0 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertices of the image in the $xy$-plane are $(1,-2), (3,0), (1,2),$ and $(-1,0).$

Drawing this region in the $xy$-plane, we get the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039710/assets/ddd14bdebe21c830396e044721811cf6b9c7bd7db067e4d0ff7d35e02a592894.png)

          

Notice that since $\det(A) = 2 >    0,$ this transformation is orientation-preserving.

e-12427.knowledge_point: Determining Whether an Affine Transformation is Orientation-Preserving
e-12427.problem:
Consider the affine transformation $\mathbf T$ defined as

$$
x = v - u-6, \qquad y = v -2u  .
$$

Let $A$ be the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $\mathbf T.$

Which of the following statements are true?

- $[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]$

- $\det(A) = 1$

- The transformation $\mathbf T$ is orientation-preserving
e-12427.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $\mathbf T:\mathbb R^2\rightarrow\mathbb R^2$ is a function of the form

$$
\mathbf x = A \mathbf u + \mathbf b,
$$

where $\mathbf x, \mathbf u,$ and $\mathbf b$ are column vectors in $\mathbb R^2,$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Let's look at each statement in turn:

- Statement I is true. Indeed, notice that the given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}v-u-6 \\ v-2u\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-u+v \\ -2u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $\mathbf T$ is $[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]$

- Statement II is true. Computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is true. Indeed, since $\det(A) > 0,$ the affine transformation $\mathbf T$ is orientation-preserving.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II, and III."

e-12436.knowledge_point: Determining the Area Scale Factor of an Affine Transformation
e-12436.problem:
Consider the affine transformation $\mathbf T,$ defined as

$$
x = 3u+4, \qquad y = 4v - 2u.
$$

What is the area scale factor of the transformation?
e-12436.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $\mathbf T:\mathbb R^2\rightarrow\mathbb R^2$ is a function of the form

$$
\mathbf x = A \mathbf u + \mathbf b,
$$

where $\mathbf x, \mathbf u,$ and $\mathbf b$ are column vectors in $\mathbb R^2,$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that the given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3u+4 \\ 4v-2u\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3u \\ -2u+4v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $\mathbf T$ is $[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}]$

Computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}
$$

So, the area scale factor of the transformation is

$$
|\det(A)| = |12| =12.
$$

after.problem:
Consider the transformation $T$ defined as

$$
x=3v+u,\,y=u-6v+3.
$$

Let $P(-2,3)$ be a point in the $uv$-plane. Suppose that the image of $P$ under the action of $T$ is the point ${P}^{′}$ in the $xy$-plane. What are the coordinates of ${P}^{′}?$
after.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that the given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3v+u \\ u-6v+3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u+3v \\ u-6v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & -6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the image of $P$ under the action of $T,$ we first create a column vector $u$ containing the coordinates of $P:$

$$
u=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Applying $T$ to $u,$ we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -17\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of ${P}^{′}$ are $(7,-17).$

An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$

Now, to find the image of $P$ under the action of $T,$ we first create a column vector $u$ containing the coordinates of $P:$

$$
u=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Applying $T$ to $u,$ we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of ${P}^{′}$ are $(9,0).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039710/assets/d947e13c2b18ce786f03636d174604dd60e715ed0ce1929ff4ac98cf91084a50.png)

Consider the rectangle $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 1}.
$$

The transformation $T$ is defined as

$$
x=3u+2v-2,\,y=2u+v-1.
$$

Which of the following gives the image of $Δ$ in the $xy$-plane under the action of $T?$
content.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that we can express the given transformation as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3u+2v-2 \\ 2u+v-1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3u+2v \\ 2u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

The transformation $T$ maps the boundary of $Δ$ to the boundary of the image. So, to find the image of $Δ,$ we find the images of each side.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039710/assets/d0103ef8cdf76a3f80bd9be6314c2a693cbf9e51fe66f95228ccce1703f6775f.png)

          

To quickly carry out this calculation, we set up the following matrices:

- The matrix $U$ containing all vertices of our square:

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ that has the same shape as $U$ and with the vector $b$ in each column:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & -2 & -2 \\ -1 & -1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

The image of $u$ under $T$ is given by $Au+b.$ So, by applying $T$ to $U,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AU+B & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & -2 & -2 \\ -1 & -1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 & 5 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & -2 & -2 \\ -1 & -1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertices of the image in the $xy$-plane are $(-2,-1),(1,1),(3,2),$ and $(0,0).$

Drawing this region in the $xy$-plane, we get the following: 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039710/assets/0b22301fac2a0d97c0f0d99b3c4d162e8965f5570522754a3e21fa124194f1c0.png)

          

Finally, since $det(A)=-1<0,$ this transformation is not orientation-preserving.

after.name: Question 16
after.problem:
Consider the affine transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
x=v-u,\,y=u+v-1.
$$

What is the area scale factor of the transformation?
after.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that the given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}v-u \\ u+v-1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-u+v \\ u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $T$ is $A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].$

Computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
det(A)=|\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|=1\cdot (-1)-1\cdot 1=-2.
$$

So, the area scale factor of the transformation is

$$
|det(A)|=|-2|=2.
$$

Consider the affine transformation T, defined as

x=2u−2v−3,y=u−v+2.

What is the area scale factor of the transformation?

EXPLANATION

An affine transformation T:R2→R2 is a function of the form x=Au+b, where x,u, and b are column vectors in R2, and A is a 2×2 matrix.

Notice that the given transformation can be expressed as [xy]=[2u−2v−3u−v+2]=[2u−2vu−v]+[−32]=[2−21−1]⏟A⋅[uv]⏟u+[−32]⏟b Therefore, the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with T is A=[2−21−1].

Computing the determinant of A, we get det(A)=|2−21−1|=2⋅(−1)−1⋅(−2)=0.

So, the area scale factor of the transformation is |det(A)|=|0|=0.

content.knowledge_point: Determining the Area Scale Factor of an Affine Transformation
content.problem:
Consider the affine transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
x=2u-2v-3,\,y=u-v+2.
$$

What is the area scale factor of the transformation?
content.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that the given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2u-2v-3 \\ u-v+2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2u-2v \\ u-v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $T$ is $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}].$

Computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
det(A)=|\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|=2\cdot (-1)-1\cdot (-2)=0.
$$

So, the area scale factor of the transformation is

$$
|det(A)|=|0|=0.
$$
